html:
SMTO-WEB-0019 — Your request changed after the research was gathered

GUID: 5aec806d-c8a6-54ba-bf17-d72180fa73da
Slug: research-contract-revision-mismatch
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • SMTO collected research for an earlier version of your request, and the request has since changed. It won't use the old research as proof for the new request, but what it already read is still saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to work from your updated request. The proof check stopped only the answer built on the earlier version of the request.
  2. If the run stops, send your full updated request again as one new message, with all the details you added along the way. One clear request lets SMTO gather research for exactly what you want now.
  3. If the run stops and an unchecked answer is acceptable to you, open the Research proof validation card shown in the run and turn off Enforce this check for this run. This publishes the answer without checking that its sources match your updated request.

What success looks like

  • The answer appears with sources that match your updated request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to reuse sources from the earlier request as proof for the new one; they were collected for different requirements.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof rejected the completion because the stored research contract digest no longer matches its contract, or the current task intent digest differs from the intent captured in the research contract.

What this means

  • Research proof finds that the stored contract digest or the current task intent differs from the captured research contract. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • Research proof finds that the stored contract digest or the current task intent differs from the captured research contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare captured contract and intent digests with the current run without relabeling old evidence.

How to fix it

  • In web_research/validation.py _validate_answer, either digest(contract) != contract_digest or intent_digest(state) != contract.intent_digest. Let the runtime rebuild research state for the revised intent (ensure() revises it) and re-acquire evidence under the new contract; keep earlier observations attributed to their original intent rather than re-binding them.
  • Reconcile the changed task intent and rebuild supported research state; preserve older observations with their original scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • Proof uses a coherent current intent and evidence remains tied to its actual source task.

What not to do

  • Do not attach evidence from an earlier intent revision to the changed requirement.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
